title: Match a pattern before searching
hook: Twelve socks, three patterns, one pile. To find one sock's partner, how many do you check?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that sorting socks by pattern first means each sock's partner is searched for in a small pile instead of the whole heap

misconception: Sorting socks into piles first is extra work and doesn't speed up pairing.
objective: In a pile you pick socks up one at a time, so the partner can be the last one you check. Sorted by pattern first, you only check the socks in that pattern's bin.

claims.text: In a pile you pick socks up one at a time, so the partner can be the last one you check. Sorted by pattern first, you only check the socks in that pattern's bin.
claims.source: Explicit geometric/arithmetic derivation in src/lib/lifehacks/home-models.ts; Candidate count=N−1 in mixed pool, ceil(N/2)−1 in one of two equal pattern groups. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md. Reset to unverified 2026-10-16 by demo-builder (r11 fix plan wave W3: new prediction line, stage and reveal; engine 2). Re-verify against the rebuilt stage. | FC pass 54 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16): DISPUTED. The numbers need an assumption the card never states and the picture contradicts. Twelve socks of three patterns is four socks per pattern, two pairs each, and the stage draws the four striped socks in a bin identically (walkthrough 03-step-2.png). Read normally (same-pattern socks match), any sock of the same pattern is a partner: in the bin the first sock you pick matches (1 check, not up to 3), and in the mixed pile the worst case is the 8 other-pattern socks plus 1 = 9, not 11. "The partner can be the last one you check" holds only if each sock has exactly one partner that is told apart from the other same-pattern pair by something not drawn. Fix (cm-lifehacks/builder, pick one): (a) say and draw that each sock has one partner (e.g. same pattern, different sizes) and keep 11/3; (b) make each pattern one pair (6 socks, 3 patterns: pile 5, bin 1); or (c) recount for interchangeable pairs (pile 9, bin 1 at 12). recall.question: Ten socks, five of each of two patterns. You pick one. How many candidates for its partner are in a mixed pile, and in its own pattern bin?
recall.why: In a mixed pile every other sock is a candidate: 10 − 1 = 9. In its pattern bin of 5, only 4 remain. The model counts candidates, not seconds, and assumes both socks are there.
